title: What If You Stood on Ceres, the Asteroid Belt's Biggest World?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Ceres? A 150-pound person would weigh four pounds.
Ceres is a dwarf planet 950 kilometers wide. Its gravity is only 0.028 times Earth's, so you could jump absurdly high.
A day lasts about nine hours. The Sun looks a third as wide as at home, and sunrise takes about 45 seconds.
Daytime hits about minus 73 degrees Celsius. At night it plunges to roughly minus 143.
Ceres is nearly three times farther from the Sun than Earth, so noon sunlight is only about 15 percent as bright.
Beneath your boots may be more water ice than all the fresh water on Earth. And one trip around the Sun takes 4.6 years.

description:
What if you stood on Ceres, the largest object in the asteroid belt? Gravity is under 3 percent of Earth's and the day lasts nine hours.
Daytime is about minus 73 degrees Celsius, and sunlight is only 15 percent as bright as at home.
What should we run through next?
